title: Accept dual symlink materialization in tests (real vs text file)
context: Default Git-for-Windows (core.symlinks=false) materializes symlinks as plain text files holding the target path, not real symlinks. Tests assumed symlinks always existed, causing failures on default Windows setups. POSIX and configured Windows (core.symlinks=true) create real symlinks.
decision: Make test assertions platform-aware: query git config core.symlinks at runtime and accept either (1) dedicated symlink-rejection errors when Git materializes symlinks, or (2) fail-closed source-layer errors (unparseable/unresolved) when Git checks symlinks out as text files. Also normalize path separators (backslash → forward slash) when comparing readlink output.
consequences: Tests now pass on default Git-for-Windows without requiring core.symlinks=true
Tests remain correct on POSIX and Windows with core.symlinks=true
Requires runtime git config query to determine expected behavior per host
Test logic more complex (conditional assertions based on host capability)
alternatives_rejected: Require core.symlinks=true for all developers (excludes default Windows workflow)
Mock git config behavior (doesn't test actual host behavior)
Always assert text-file behavior (misses real symlink guard on POSIX)
